findings.title: TeamViewer urges users to patch severe flaws as soon as possible
findings.summary_md: Remote access software company TeamViewer warned customers on Tuesday to immediately patch a set of high-severity vulnerabilities affecting its client and host software. The highest-severity flaw is a remote session access control bypass (CVE-2026-92370) stemming from an improper access control weakness in TeamViewer Full Client and Host software for Windows, Linux, and macOS that could let remote threat actors perform unauthorized actions leading to remote code execution. The other four issues are a path traversal (CVE-2026-19743), a heap-based buffer overflow (CVE-2026-92368), a TOCTOU race condition (CVE-2026-92369), and an improper path validation (CVE-2026-92371). TeamViewer strongly recommended that all users update to the latest available version as soon as possible.

findings.title: TeamViewer just told every desktop owner to update before the weekend
findings.summary_md: TeamViewer published a rare update-as-soon-as-possible advisory covering five high-severity flaws in Full Client and Host on Windows, Linux, and macOS. The lead issue is a remote session access-control bypass that can let an attacker perform unauthorized actions leading to remote code execution. Fixed builds land at version 15.82 and supported maintenance and legacy lines. TeamViewer said it had no evidence of public exploit code or active exploitation yet.

findings.title: TeamViewer Patches 5 Flaws, Worst Hits CVSS 8.8 [2026]
findings.summary_md: TeamViewer fixed 5 vulnerabilities, including a CVSS 8.8 access-control bypass (CVE-2026-92370), in its September 29, 2026 bulletin TV-2026-1010. The bulletin covers Full Client and Host for Windows, Linux, and macOS. The article notes TeamViewer's 2016 account-takeover complaints and 2024 APT29 corporate network intrusion as separate historical incidents not related to this product flaw. TV-2026-1010 is a vendor-disclosed, coordinated set of product vulnerabilities with CVE identifiers and a shipped fix.
